sections.title: Capacity arrives as physical packages, not a smooth curve
sections.dek: The entity ramp and process flow expose the discreteness and attrition hidden by aggregate forecasts.

body.text: This synthetic example treats the 2.5D package as the unit of analysis. Capacity expands in steps, while lots are lost between input, assembly, qualification and shipment.
All figures in this demonstration are synthetic and exist only to test the plugin.

charts.title: Nameplate capacity triples in two synthetic steps
charts.subtitle: Synthetic period-end capacity; thousand packages per month
charts.note: One glyph represents two thousand packages of monthly capacity.

charts.title: The physical flow narrows before shipment
charts.subtitle: Synthetic lots moving through the package system, 2026-Q2

charts.title: Signals move from demand to qualified capacity with a lag
charts.subtitle: Synthetic causal hypothesis; fact-bound signal, lag, threshold and sparklines
charts.note: Edges encode the report's analytical hypothesis and do not establish statistical causality.

sections.annotation: The entity view makes capacity additions legible; the flow view prevents the reader from treating nameplate capacity as sellable output.
takeaways: Track physical bottlenecks separately from announced capacity.
Do not equate installed tools with qualified shipment volume.

sections.title: Competitive advantage changes by dimension and layer
sections.dek: A matrix supports multi-dimensional scanning; a value stack preserves the physical order of the package.

body.text: Synthetic vendor scores show that leadership is not one-dimensional. The value pool also concentrates in later assembly, test and qualification steps.

charts.title: Vendor leadership rotates across technical dimensions
charts.subtitle: Synthetic comparable score; actual 0–100 scale

charts.title: Qualification captures the largest synthetic value layer
charts.subtitle: Indexed value pool; layers sum to 100

sections.annotation: Heat intensity supports scanning, but every cell retains its number. The stack is ordered by the physical assembly rather than by visual size.
takeaways: Benchmark by constraint, not by a single composite score.
Map economics onto the physical package before discussing market share.

sections.title: History explains the setup; probabilities expose the judgment
sections.dek: The timeline separates sequence from forecast, while the odds board makes scenario assumptions explicit.

body.title: Interpretation boundary
body.text: A probability is an analyst judgment as of a date, not a reported future fact.

sections.annotation: The visual grammar deliberately separates dated observations from forward-looking odds.
takeaways: Tie every probability to a horizon and observable trigger.
Update the odds board when evidence changes, not on a fixed aesthetic cadence.

sections.title: Use conventional charts only when exact reading is the task
sections.dek: A line chart is justified for the demand-supply path; paired bars are justified for explicit scenario comparisons.

body.text: The line chart is not a default. It appears here because the exact gap across ordered years matters. The paired bars exist because two named cases must be compared directly.

sections.annotation: The chart form follows the reading task: ordered path for trends, explicit pairs for scenarios.
takeaways: Conventional charts are tools of precision, not default decoration.
Keep scenario values visibly distinct from reported observations.

methodology: All values are synthetic and were chosen to exercise the plugin's validation, chart routing and evidence drawer.
The example preserves numeric machine values separately from display formatting.
Probabilities are illustrative analyst judgments with an explicit as-of date and horizon.
Causal-horizon edges encode an analytical hypothesis and do not establish statistical causality.
disclosures: This is a software demonstration, not investment research or a factual semiconductor dataset.
No synthetic number should be copied into a real report without replacement and source verification.
Cover views were generated with Image 2 from one canonical identity anchor; the bundled engineering schematic remains an explicit fallback and is not the active renderer.
